verses.author: model_A
verses.text: A boat leaves the harbor before anyone is awake to see it go.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Someone finds the rope still warm from a hand
and coils it anyway, not knowing why.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Salt dries on the dock boards, white as breath—
a gull tests the empty air where the mast was,
then decides not to follow.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The dock boards creak once, twice, settling flat—
someone counts the nails still holding fast
and finds the count comes out even.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The tide erases what the count could not—
a child draws the number in wet sand,
watches it go soft, then gone.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Someone else picks up the chalk instead—
draws a boat where the tide line used to be,
gives it three windows and calls it done.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The chalk boat sits above the water's reach—
a dog sniffs the hull, decides it's harmless,
lifts its leg at the third window anyway.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Someone laughs, then someone else complains—
the chalk is smudged now past all fixing,
so they call it weathered instead of ruined.
